Anya: FYI observed a regression on prod-sim when enabling flash-attn + TP8 for decoder-only models, ~25-35% worse p95 on single-token decode.
Marcus: ugh. same model and input distribution as before?
Anya: yes, nothing else changed in the workload. small batches (mostly B=1/2) and long context.
Tina: can you paste the profiler output? nvprof/nsys traces would help.
Anya: attached snippets from nsys — see the weird gap pattern around qkv all-gather.
Anya: ```
# timeline simplified
GPU0: compute(QKV kernel) -> wait 1.8ms -> all-gather(128KB) -> compute(attn)
GPU1: compute(QKV) -> all-gather starts earlier -> compute(attn) -> wait for recv -> stalled compute tails
# many layers show small, frequent all-gathers that block compute overlap
```
Lee: sounds like we switched to an all-gather pattern that emits many small messages per head/chunk. overhead is killing us at small batch sizes.
Marcus: did kernel selection pick flash-attn for those seq lengths? flash sometimes chooses different tiling which affects how QKV are sharded.
Anya: yes, runtime picked fused flash kernel for attn but TP layout still does per-tensor partitioning which forces QKV all-gathers per micro-batch.
Tina: so two issues: (1) batching heuristics creating many micro-batches, (2) QKV layout + TP producing many small all-gathers that can't overlap.
perf-bot: perf-report uploaded: https://redwood-internal/reports/1732101123/trace.html :thumbsup:
Marcus: quick checklist: 1) how we partition QKV across TP dims 2) whether all-gather is aggregated by head-chunk 3) kernel choice fallback when comm overhead > threshold
Lee: I think we can mitigate in two ways: change KV cache layout to shard along sequence (local first) so decoder doesn't all-gather on every step, or batch up small all-gathers into a single NCCL op (aggregate heads).
Tina: aggregation sounds doable: merge adjacent all-gathers into a single round if the combined size < X and the latency saving > Y. Could be a runtime batching heuristic: if B * head_chunk < threshold -> merge.
Anya: also saw that for certain layer sizes flash-attn is slower because its internal workspace forcing extra copies with TP split. If we add a per-layer decision: if TP and seq<64 and B<=2, prefer non-fused kernel with a larger compute overlap, we recover p95.
Marcus: do we have an automated profiler rule to flip kernels when comm/compute overlap predicted < 0.3?
Tina: not yet, but we can compute an estimate: comm_time = alpha + beta * bytes, compute_time = FLOPS / perf. We can estimate overlap by simulating schedule. Add a cheap heuristic in kernel-selector.
Lee: I prototyped an async all-gather aggregator yesterday: it coalesces small NCCL ops and launches them non-blocking so compute can proceed. In microbenchmarks it reduced stall by ~40% for 32-128KB messages.
Anya: nice. Would that break existing KV cache consistency for decode streaming?
Lee: no, semantics preserved — it's just combining ops that were logically independent. We still maintain ordering.
Marcus: sequence-based local KV shard also attractive: store most recent tokens locally and only sync on checkpointed windows, not every step. But that's more invasive and affects memory layout.
Tina: rolling plan: (1) add kernel-selector heuristic to prefer non-fused kernel for tiny batches/seqs (2) land NCCL coalescing path (3) experiment with local-first KV shard for decode.
Anya: can we run an A/B on staging with tp=8, B=1/2, seq=512 to validate? I can start a job matrix.
perf-bot: test-matrix queued: job ids [id-1732101201, id-1732101202]
Marcus: also add a perf regression alert threshold to the console: if p95 delta > 15% after deploy, auto-rollback candidate.
Tina: noted. I'll draft kernel-selector PR with microbench numbers. Marcus, can you review the NCCL coalescing change?
Marcus: yep, will review. Lee, can you include the microbench script you used?
Lee: posting snippet: ```bash
# microbench for small all-gathers
for size in 16384 32768 65536 131072; do
  python bench_nccl.py --size $size --repeats 500
done
```
Lee: output: 32KB -> avg 0.12ms per op, coalesced 0.07ms per op equivalent.
Anya: thanks team. I'll run the staged A/B and report back with traces. If we recover p95 we'll flip on the coalesce by default behind a flag.
Tina: one more: add telemetry keys so console graphs can split total all-gather time vs compute time per-layer. That will help future kernel selector tuning.
Anya: good call. I'll add metric names: `rpc.all_gather_ms`, `kernel.compute_ms`, `kernel.wait_ms` in the rollout.
Marcus: extra thought: for flash-attn edgecases, we should add a fuzz harness that varies TP split and seq to catch these regressions pre-deploy.
Anya: agreed. I'll open a ticket and tag eng-sre.
perf-bot: ticket created: INF-2419 - "TP+Flash perf regression harness"
Lee: cool. I'll attach the microtrace to the ticket.
Anya: end-to-end plan in comments, thanks all. :rocket:
